newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom to issue offshore bonds.
newsitem.headline: Telekom to issue offshore bonds.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd said on Tuesday that it expects to issue about $350 million in offshore bonds to finance its investment in South African telecommunications utility Telkom.

Answering questions from reporters, Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali, Telekom's chief executive officer, said about 70 percent of the financing for the investment would be raised through offshore bonds which "would amount to $350 million".
Asked when Telekom was likely to raise the funds, Mohamed Said replied: "Anytime between now and the end of this year."
In March, the national telecommunications firm said it would invest around $504 million in a U.S.-Malaysian consortium that is buying a 30 percent stake in Telkom.
Telekom Malaysia's own stake in the privatisation deal amounts to 12 percent.
For the balance of the 30 percent financing, Mohamad Said said the funds would come from internal sources, saying it would be from "what we have in our pockets".

When asked if Telekom was looking to acquire a stake in private television company Sistem Televisyen Malaysia Bhd (TV3), he said, "I don't know if TV3 shares are for offer. They have made no offer (to us). If there is an offer, we will consider it very seriously."
Rumours that Telekom was eyeing a 20 percent stake in TV3 had circulated in the market late last year.
Mohamed Said explained the rationale for looking at TV3 would centre on the "convergence between entertainment, media and telecommunications".
"TV3 is very attractive because they have media and entertainment in one shot. If such an opportunity arises it would be like killing two birds with one stone," he said.
